questions.q: A writing team wants to work the way Trier and Vogt describe. Where should they start?
choices: With a beat sheet, then cast characters to fit each beat
With a logline tested on an audience before any characters exist
With long conversations about life and the characters, arriving at plot late
With the ending, then work backwards to the inciting incident
questions.explain: They have said they talk for a long time, often about life rather than scenes, and let material and characters come before plot.

questions.q: A writer's voice-over says, over a shot of a man crying, 'He was very sad.' What would Trier say is wrong with it?
choices: It only repeats what the image shows; narration should contrast with the picture or add what it can't show
Voice-over must always be spoken by the protagonist in the first person
Narration belongs only in the opening and closing minutes
It's fine, as long as the actor recording it is well known
questions.explain: Trier told Seventh Row (2016) that voice-over is a cop-out when it tells us what the film isn't showing, and earns its place when it contrasts with the image.

questions.q: Oslo, August 31st opens with old footage of the city under anonymous voices, each beginning 'I remember'. What does this opening do?
choices: It sets up a mystery about which of the voices is the killer
It frames the film as memory and makes the city a presence Anders will walk through
It provides a cold open with the story's inciting incident
It replaces the need for any further voice-over
questions.explain: The voices make Oslo a place of memories before we meet Anders, who spends one day walking through his own past in the city.

questions.q: In The Worst Person in the World, Julie flicks a light switch and all of Oslo freezes while she runs to meet another man. In the terms of Story vs. telling, what is this?
choices: An ellipsis: time skipped between chapters
A flashback revealing her childhood wound
A pause made literal: the world stops while the telling continues, showing her wish to delay consequences
A false ending before the real climax
questions.explain: Narrative pause usually means the story stops while description continues; here the pause becomes visible and expresses what Julie wants.

questions.q: Why does a film like The Worst Person in the World use titled chapters?
choices: To mark the five acts that Freytag's pyramid requires
Because each chapter is written by a different writer
To signal commercial breaks for television broadcast
To make jumps in time honest and give the film a wry, novelistic voice
questions.explain: The prologue, twelve chapters and epilogue let time leap between sections, and the titles comment on Julie with gentle irony.

questions.q: Sentimental Value introduces Nora on an opening night when stage fright makes her try to flee. What principle is at work?
choices: Introduce a character on an extreme day, when they're least in control, to show at once what the story is about
Save the cat: make the hero likeable through a kind act
Delay the protagonist's entrance until the second act
Open with the climax and then flash back
questions.explain: On Scriptnotes (2026), Trier said he prefers introducing characters on an extreme day rather than an ordinary one.

questions.q: Trier said Sentimental Value became 'polyphonic' while he and Vogt were writing. What changed?
choices: They added a chorus that sings between scenes
They realized the daughter's story also needed the father's point of view
They cut the film into twelve chapters
They replaced the dialogue with voice-over
questions.explain: He told John August it began as the daughter's story and grew into a film with several centres of feeling, including the father's.

ideas: Cinema is the art form of memory: open with voices remembering a place before the story begins.
Voice-over earns its place only when it contrasts with the image instead of explaining it.
Introduce a character on their most extreme day, not an ordinary one.
Let a city stop dead so a heroine can avoid a choice for one stolen day.
